Subject: Sentinel Health discovery — recommended next steps & model scorecard

Hi Ari (and team),

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — really helpful to see the 2 primary intents you need (diagnosis-categorization + patient-sentiment triage) and the latency / cost constraints you called out. Per our discussion, I pulled together a concise scorecard + proposed decision path so we can move straight to a lightweight eval. Attached: "sentinel_fit_scorecard.xlsx" (one-pager with metrics & thresholds) and "prompt_bundle_sentinel_v1.json" (500 case prompt bundle sample).

High-level proposal (short):
- Run a 1-week A/B evaluation across three candidates:
  1) Open model A (Llama-2-Chat-70B, HF baseline, full precision) — expected quality ceiling, higher cost/latency.
  2) Open model B (Llama-2-Chat-13B quantized + Redwood runtime optimizations) — good cost/latency balance.
  3) Your current proprietary baseline ("SentinelML-v1") — what you used in prod today (we'll treat as control).
- Goals / acceptance criteria (see scorecard):
  - Intent accuracy (micro-avg F1) >= baseline - tolerance of 2% absolute (parity gate).
  - Safety / hallucination threshold: hallucination rate <= 1.5% on targeted QA checks.
  - Latency: p50 <= 150ms for short prompts, p95 <= 400ms.
  - Cost target: < $0.75 per 1k tokens (approx) for production path, but we'll evaluate tradeoffs.
- Eval details:
  - Use the attached prompt bundle (500 representative cases, holdout 100 for blind QA).
  - Autograde with labeled intents + heuristics; sample-blind human review for safety/regression signals.
  - If open model reaches parity by the 2% tolerance and passes safety gating, we recommend a controlled rollout (canary with auto-rollback).

Links / artifacts:
- Quick benchmark summary (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/sales/sentinel/benchmarks/summary-2025-08
- Prompt bundle: attached and mirrored at https://drive.redwood.com/teams/sales/sentinel/prompt-sets/prompt_bundle_sentinel_v1.json

Next steps I recommend from here:
1) Confirm the 500-case bundle is representative (we can iterate).
2) Grant Karthik (SE) read access to a small sample of de-identified logs (10k requests) to calibrate latency/kv cache sizing.
3) Kick off a 7-day A/B run once we have access — we can stand up the eval in Dedicated sandbox or hosted mode depending on your compliance needs.

Ari — are you OK with the gating thresholds in the attached scorecard? If so I'll loop in Karthik & Marissa to schedule the test and finalize the eval script.

Thanks,

All — quick plan below, happy to iterate. I'll attach the eval script and a short infra estimate in the next email.

Evaluation plan (7-day A/B):
- Candidates: control (SentinelML-v1), Open-A = Llama-2-Chat-70B (FP), Open-B = Llama-2-Chat-13B (4-bit quantized with Redwood runtime).
- Test set: 500 cases from prompt_bundle_sentinel_v1.json, holdout 100 for blind human review.
- Auto-metrics: intent micro-F1, triage exact-match, answer length deviation, hallucination_count (heuristic: factual-entity mismatch vs. KB).
- Human review: random n=100 blind; 2 annotators per sample, adjudicate disagreements.
- Acceptance gates:
  - Parity: Open model considered acceptable if intent micro-F1 >= baseline - 0.02 (i.e., within 2% absolute).
  - Safety: hallucination_count <= baseline + 0.01 (we recommend 1% absolute tighter than the proposed 1.5%; see notes).
  - Latency: p50 <= 150ms (us-east-1), p95 <= 400ms. If latency exceeded by >25% we flag for infra tuning.
- Regression policy: any drop > 3% absolute on micro-F1 or safety > +1% triggers manual stop and rollback.
- Data handling: we'll run in hosted sandbox with logs retained 30 days by default; we can toggle retention and disable KV persistence for PII-sensitive traces.
- Deliverables by EOD Fri: eval-script (Python + curl harness), infra-sizing (GPU type + estimated token throughput), initial runbook for canary + auto-rollback.

Ari — please share the de-identified 7-day sample when ready (S3 link or shared Drive) and confirm us-east-1 as the primary region. Also confirm whether your QA team wants the human review instructions in CSV or via a short Google Form.

Marissa — I'm happy to use the tighter safety gate (1% absolute) if that's our conservative default; will call that out in the runbook.
